key_insight: An interpretable finite-element inverse framework identifies relative spatial variations in multiple constitutive parameters of 3D heterogeneous hyperelastic materials from displacement fields alone.
engineering_relevance: Mapping material-property variations could support characterization of graded composites and heterogeneous biological tissues.
method: Leverages linearity of the hyperelastic inverse problem in the constitutive parameters.
Optimizes constitutive parameters directly at the finite-element level.
evidence_signal: Validation on 3D synthetic and 2D experimental benchmarks covers heterogeneous, graded, and anisotropic hyperelastic materials, with reported acceptable accuracy and substantially lower computational time than recent deep-learning frameworks.
watch_item: The framework recovers relative parameter variations; absolute property calibration and robustness to noisy 3D experimental displacement data require further assessment.
paper_title: Interpretable identification of constitutive parameter field for three-dimensional heterogeneous and graded hyperelastic materials from full-field displacements
